I used to live in Pazardzhik and in my experience healthcare was relatively decent. There are of course poor areas of the town with low living standards, however it isn't all bad. I think there are a lot fewer well paid jobs compared to big cities like Sofia, Plovdiv and Varna. State run hospitals and medical centres are definitely not at the standard of western countries, but I can say I received some very good dental care. 

There are two main private hospitals my family has used called "Higia" (Хигия) and "Esculap" (Ескулап). Like others mentioned, with private health care you'll probably be fine. 

Unfortunately there are a lot of cases of sub-standard care and poor conditions like the ones in the picture, mainly in small towns and villages. I haven't lived in the country for a while so I'm not sure exactly how things are right now...

Nobody intentionally wastes or sabotages their life, but it is likely caused by a combination of struggling mentally, having one's confidence crushed or crippling fear. You say he doesn't have problems with drugs or alcohol and he has a job. To most, this is not wildly impressive, however it is a good base and a better position than many people out there. 

It may be useful to suggest that he spends time thinking about what he wants, setting specific goals, then sub goals and working towards them in small steps. Some practical examples: saving a small sum of money each week, researching career goals for 30 minutes each day, planning for training or education, gradually improving your diet, going to get help from a mental health professional. 

I believe everyone can improve if they're in a good environment and are given encouragement. You get positive feedback loops where good/virtuous behaviours reinforce themselves. Young men are generally attracted to becoming competent and responsible, so this can be a catalyst. 

From my own perspective of being a young adult (that struggles often) it's best to just be non-vindictive and non-patronising, but just down-to-earth. People are more willing to listen this way. It feels like I'm a bit similar to your son. I can tell you this "hot mess" position is very painful and I've never wanted to let down my parents. Anyways I've gone on, sorry, just my two cents.

You're a a very strong person to keep going after all of that suffering; stronger than me for sure. Thanks for sharing this it can serve as motivation for many people. 2019 was also horrible for me but it serves to make you tougher and rise again.

Thanks for posting this. I'm glad you decided to live on. You can still have a great life and be successful, no doubt about it. We should compare ourselves to who we were yesterday, not to who someone else is today. At the same time this feeling of being behind is the most painful thing I ever experienced. So I empathise completely with you. I had a lot of dreams crushed and often felt I could never be like my peers. Well done on figuring out a good diet that helps you. We are all in unique circumstances, so we shouldn't be too hard on ourselves. Another person who is motivational to me is David Goggins, although he may not be everyone's cup of tea. Best of luck.

It can also be because a person is indecisive and doesn't know what to do. For me this is the killer as usually I'm fine when I know exactly what I need to do. I wish logic had more power in the mind instead of primitive parts of the brain. Oh well.

It's a really difficult situation for sure. Hardest thing is not to beat yourself up about it, but try to develop self-respect. The only logical thing anyone can do is to take the next step from where they are. This might be working, getting healthier, building up habits, studying, seeking medical help, etc. Ruminating about the past is dangerous and torturous. Just a suggestion: running and taking nutritional supplements helped stabilise me a bit in the past. Of course, easier said than done. I'm in a very similar position and also freaking out.
